topic: ? and # for paucal adjuncts with high-degree verbs
claim: “Paucal adjuncts tend not to occur with verbs which inherently involve a high degree”, illustrated with He liked / ?adored her a little and It had slightly damaged / #ruined her prospects.
evidence_summary: One reason covers both examples, but they carry different marks. The notational conventions (p. xii) use ? for questionable grammaticality and # for semantically or pragmatically anomalous.
finding: Low to medium confidence: one stated restriction, two status categories. The defence that ruin is lexically maximal, so that slightly ruined is a contradiction while adored her a little is a milder clash, partly works, but the text doesn’t say the two cases differ in kind.
inference: Does one degree restriction call for one status mark?

evidence.passage: §11, p. 723. “Paucal adjuncts tend not to occur with verbs which inherently involve a high degree”
evidence.example: He liked / ?adored her a little; It had slightly damaged / #ruined her prospects.
evidence.establishes: Two status marks for one stated restriction.
